current_focus.summary: Bobby confirmed the bounded platform-neutral transfer-list read model. Each query explicitly selects Open or Done for one explicit pool and either one active location or All Locations. One-location scope includes incoming and outgoing transfers; All Locations returns each matching transfer once. Archived endpoints remain out of normal selectors but stay visibly identified when relevant to an active location, while transfers whose endpoints are both archived remain archive-only. Open is urgency-ordered by expected dispatch or arrival; Done is newest terminal event first. Each row is a compact transfer summary with full line, note, actor, receipt, warning, and audit detail left to existing detail reads. Default pagination is 50, maximum 100, with a stable opaque cursor. Search, alternate sorting, GUI, CLI, HTTP/auth, integrations, schema migration, deployment, partial receiving, and Received reversion remain excluded.

decisions.choice: Each query explicitly requests exactly one view: Open or Done. The human UI initially selects Open, then requests Done when the user changes tabs. Open returns Created and In-transit transfers; Done returns Received and Canceled transfers. Inventory never infers a remembered tab.

decisions.question: Does one transfer-list query return both Open and Done, or does the caller explicitly request one view?
decisions.rationale: Separate views keep their ordering and pagination independent, avoid loading potentially large completed history when an operator needs active work, and still preserve Katana's two-tab behavior at the client.

decisions.choice: A one-location list includes a transfer when the selected location is either its origin or its destination. The row retains both endpoints so the client can show it as outgoing or incoming relative to the selection. An unrelated transfer between two other locations is excluded. All Locations returns every matching transfer in the pool once, never once per endpoint.

decisions.question: When one location is selected, which stock transfers belong in that location's Open or Done list?
decisions.rationale: Operators responsible for one location need to see both stock leaving it and stock expected to arrive there. Returning each transfer once avoids duplicate rows while retaining the full route.

decisions.choice: Archived locations stay absent from the normal location selector. A transfer remains visible when the selected active location is one of its endpoints, even if the other endpoint was later archived; that endpoint is visibly marked Archived. All Locations includes a transfer once when at least one endpoint is active. A transfer whose origin and destination are both archived leaves the normal lists and remains accessible through explicit archived-location history.

decisions.question: How should normal transfer lists handle history involving a location that was later archived?
decisions.rationale: This preserves complete incoming and outgoing audit history for active locations while honoring the prior out-of-sight archive rule and avoiding dead archived locations in normal selectors.

decisions.choice: Open is ordered by the next operational date from earliest to latest, with overdue work first: a Created transfer uses expectedDispatchDate and an In-transit transfer uses expectedArrivalDate. Equal dates use most recently updated first, then permanent transfer ID as the stable tie-breaker. Done is ordered by terminal date from newest to oldest: receivedDate for Received and canceledAt for Canceled, with the same deterministic tie-breakers. V1 defines this one useful default order rather than adding sort controls.

decisions.question: What deterministic default order should Open and Done transfer lists use?
decisions.rationale: Operational urgency should not be buried by a recently edited future transfer, while completed history is normally inspected newest first. Stable tie-breakers prevent duplicates or omissions when paging.

decisions.choice: Each list result contains one compact row per transfer: editable human reference, lifecycle status, origin and destination location identities with archived status when applicable, distinct product-line count, and the dates relevant to that view. Open rows include created, expected-dispatch, and expected-arrival dates. Received rows include actual dispatched and received dates; Canceled rows include created and canceled dates. Full SKU quantities, note, warnings, actors, receipts, and complete retained dates remain in the existing transfer/detail and audit reads rather than expanding every line in the list.

decisions.question: How much transfer and item detail belongs in each Open or Done list row?
decisions.rationale: One transfer can contain many products. A compact operational index remains scannable and paginates by transfer, while the authoritative detail read already owns exact lines and stock context.

decisions.choice: The read model returns at most 50 transfers by default and permits a caller-requested limit up to 100. It returns an opaque next cursor when more matching transfers exist, or null at the end. The client can request the next batch without changing pool, location scope, or Open/Done view. Pagination follows the locked deterministic order and never uses fragile numbered offsets. V1 does not add alternate sorting, free-text search, or an exact total-count query to this slice.

decisions.question: How should a transfer list load when a pool contains more transfers than should be returned at once?
decisions.rationale: Most active lists arrive in one response, while years of Done history stay bounded. Cursor pagination avoids duplicate or skipped rows caused by inserting newer transfers ahead of a numbered page.
